card.name: Administer before route words
card.fires_on: The word "administer(ed)" in route-of-administration warnings, especially "Do not administer" before a route such as intravenously or systemically. It also fires on a few other words just before a route term.

modes.label: Do not administer
modes.description: The verb administer in a restriction naming the only allowed route, just before a route word.
modes.example: Do NOT<< administer>> by any other route.

modes.label: Administered systemically
modes.description: The word administered or absorbed where a route or body-wide effect is expected next.
modes.example: Myelosuppression is possible if valrubicin intravesical solution is inadvertently<< administered>> systemically or if significant systemic exposure occurs

modes.label: Linking words before route
modes.description: A small word like either or and between two routes of giving a drug.
modes.example: When cytarabine is administered both intrathecally<< and>> intravenously within a few days,

card.writes: It pushes the model toward the word "system" (as in systemic or nervous system) and its Chinese equivalents.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a warning where the text is about to name a route of giving a drug, such as intravenous or systemic.
